title: Monoculture Practice Impacts Biodiversity
definition: Monoculture is the agricultural practice of growing a single crop, plant, or livestock species, variety, or breed in a field or farming system at a time. It leads to ecological simplification, reducing genetic diversity and ecosystem resilience.
importanceInUpsc: Directly linked to GS Paper III (Environment/Agriculture), specifically 'Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation'. Frequently tested in the context of food security vs. ecological sustainability.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Monoculture Practice Impacts Biodiversity.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Ecology and Biodiversity
